details: Shieber. It uses context-free grammar rules and feature constraints on these rules.

explainer.lead: PATR-II is a linguistic formalism used in computational linguistics, developed by Stuart M. Shieber, that combines context-free grammar rules with feature constraints. It matters because it lets grammars carry agreement and other grammatical information that plain context-free rules cannot express.

tiers.eli5: It is a grammar recipe book where each rule comes with extra conditions, so a sentence only counts if features like number or gender line up.
tiers.practitioner: Computational linguists use it to write grammars whose rules are filtered by feature constraints, typically with unification. The pitfall is that unconstrained feature propagation can make parsing costly or allow unintended feature combinations.
tiers.paperLevel: PATR-II uses context-free grammar rules plus feature constraints on those rules; a rule applies only when its feature constraints are satisfied. Expressiveness and parsing cost depend on how the constraints and unification are formulated.

explainer.example: A rule combining a subject and a verb is allowed only if their number features match, so a plural subject cannot combine with a singular verb form.
